articles.title: Your AI Agent Pipeline Wastes Tokens on the Wrong Tiles
articles.excerpt: The viral Maya pyramid story sounds like a win for AI agents. A team pointed dozens of agents at NASA LiDAR data and found a structure in days. The unglamorous part is why it worked at all: they did n…
articles.body: The viral Maya pyramid story sounds like a win for AI agents. A team pointed dozens of agents at NASA LiDAR data and found a structure in days. The unglamorous part is why it worked at all: they did not let agents read the whole forest. They triaged tiles first, then spent expensive model calls on candidates. By the end of this article you'll be able to structure a multi-agent scan over a large raster dataset without burning your token budget on empty ground. Naive agents scan everything The obvious approach: tile the LiDAR hillshade into images, ask a vision model "is there a structure here?", repeat for every tile. For a survey area of a few hundred square kilometers at 1-meter resolution, that's millions of tiles.

articles.title: Invoice Templates by Industry: What Actually Changes (and What Never Should)
articles.excerpt: Invoice Templates by Industry: What Actually Changes (and What Never Should) A freelance developer I know once downloaded a construction invoice template because it looked more professional than her b…
articles.body: Invoice Templates by Industry: What Actually Changes (and What Never Should) A freelance developer I know once downloaded a construction invoice template because it looked more professional than her blank one. She sent it to a small agency with the retention line still on it — 5% held back until practical completion. The client paid happily, then asked when the retention would be released. Nobody knew. The template had introduced a contract term neither party had agreed to. That is the trap: templates look like formatting, but they carry contract language. The blocks are neutral. The words are not.

articles.title: International Invoices and Currency: Getting Paid Across Borders Without Surprises
articles.excerpt: International Invoices and Currency: Getting Paid Across Borders Without Surprises The quote was in dollars. The client pays in euros. The bank takes a fee, the exchange rate has moved since the invoi…
articles.body: International Invoices and Currency: Getting Paid Across Borders Without Surprises The quote was in dollars. The client pays in euros. The bank takes a fee, the exchange rate has moved since the invoice date, and the amount that lands is three percent short. The invoice simply never said what "paid" meant. Cross-border invoicing is not difficult in the way that tax law is difficult. It is difficult the way a checklist is: more fields, more intermediaries, more ways for a detail to go missing. Most problems are omissions, and most omissions can be fixed before the invoice is sent. Decide the currency before you quote Invoice in the currency you quoted. If you quoted in USD, bill in USD. Converting at payment time moves the exchange risk onto you.

articles.body: An RTX 3080 running Cyberpunk 2077 went from roughly 42 FPS to 74 with 2X frame generation and 120 with 4X. Those are numbers posted by user fogoticus (via TechPowerUp), not our own benchmark. The mod behind this is dlssg_for_sm86 , also called DLSSG SM86, by GitHub developer sdli1995. It enables NVIDIA's own DLSS frame generation on older RTX cards. This guide follows version 0.4.1 , current as of November 2026. Treat it as an experiment for offline games, with a backup and a clear way back. What it does, and why NVIDIA restricted it Frame generation inserts AI-generated frames between rendered frames, making motion look smoother. A higher displayed frame rate does not mean the game responds faster to input.

For years people talked about them like mythical creatures: someone who could write perfect React at 9am, debug a database at lunch, and configure a production cluster by dinner. articles.title: Running several coding agents in one window: what to check
articles.excerpt: Running several command-line coding agents at once can save time, but only if you can see what each one is doing. The failure mode is not the model; it is losing track of which agent is waiting for ap…
articles.body: Running several command-line coding agents at once can save time, but only if you can see what each one is doing. The failure mode is not the model; it is losing track of which agent is waiting for approval, which one is stuck, and which one already changed a file. Put the queue in one place If every agent has its own terminal, you are the queue. A shared task list with one approval gate keeps the work visible and prevents two agents from editing the same file at the same time. Keep approvals explicit An agent that can run any command without review is faster until it is not. A single approval point per task is easier to audit than a separate confirmation for every tool call. Keep the logs local Task history should stay on your machine.

articles.title: We can't see Fast Radio Bursts but we can now hear them thanks to a Finnish Cathedral
articles.excerpt: Fast radio bursts are invisible, but a composer has turned thousands of them into sound at a Finnish cathedral, where a choir will sing along on Nov. 21.
articles.body: Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 11, 1966: NASA launches Gemini 12 mission with astronaut icons Buzz Aldrin and Jim Lovell aboard
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program to land humans on the moon. Gemini 12 was the last mission of the Gemini program. It had two astronauts on board: Jim Lovell and Buzz Aldrin . NASA wanted to send humans to the moon. But first, it needed to make sure crews had the right skills, like docking vehicles in space and taking spacewalks. Before Gemini 12, astronauts struggled with spacewalks because there weren't enough handholds on their spacecraft. NASA made some spacewalk changes for Gemini 12. Aldrin performed three spacewalks and spent more than five hours working in space with no major problems. Gemini 12 also successfully docked to an unpiloted Agena booster that launched the same day.

articles.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
articles.excerpt: For over a century astronomers have speculated that comets could have delivered organic molecules necessary for life to Earth, but new modeling shows these molecules wouldn't have survived impact.
articles.body: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space?

articles.body: The coming launch bottleneck has ramped up demand for a rocket that has yet to leave the ground. Rocket Lab announced on Monday (Nov. 9) that it recently raised the price of a Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million — an increase of more than 25%, for a ride on a rocket that's set to debut in 2027. "Launch is extremely constrained, and that is exactly the situation we predicted," Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck said on Monday during the company's third-quarter earnings call.

M30 is a globular star cluster located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth. (Image credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G. Piotto, A. Sarajedini) What is it? The exquisite image released by ESA on Nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus.
